**🎫 Ticket compliance analysis 🔶** **[115](https://github.com/fixture-owner/snaptally/issues/115) - Partially compliant** Compliant requirements: - Calls `normalizeMerchant` client-side on merchant selection. - Uses `recentTransactions` to find most common matching tuple for unknown merchants. - Auto-updates bucket, subcategory, and card on merchant selection. - Manual category and card overrides are preserved. - "Trader Joe's" -> Fixed Costs / Groceries. - "Starbucks" history -> Amex Gold / Guilt-Free / Coffee & Snacks. - Manual category tap overrides inference. - Unit tests cover canonical rules, history, and override preservation. Non-compliant requirements: - IndexedDB outbox cache fallback is not implemented (only `recentTransactions`). Requires further human verification: - Sub-5-second repeat entry UX in a real mobile browser. - Behavior when the recent feed is empty (only five transactions loaded) for merchants with older history.
⏱️ Estimated effort to review: 4 🔵🔵🔵🔵⚪
🧪 PR contains tests
🔒 No security concerns identified
⚡ Recommended focus areas for review

Architectural Verdict ARCHITECTURALLY SOUND BUT OVERBUILT. The underlying use case (fewer taps for repeat merchants) is real and the simplest mechanism — the existing `normalizeMerchant` rules plus the already-loaded recent feed — is the right one; no new services, caches, or network hops were added, which is good. However the implementation carries significant incidental state: four new flags (`categoryManuallySelected`, `cardManuallySelected`, `merchantInferenceRequested`, plus two baseline snapshots) and a "restore previous selections" behavior that the ticket never asked for. The ticket only requires inference + manual override preservation. The baseline-restore logic is the main source of the complexity and the failure modes below. Strongest simpler alternative: drop `inferredCategoryBaseline`/`inferredCardBaseline` and the restore-on-unmatched-merchant behavior; keep only the two manual-selection flags and re-run inference on each merchant change. That satisfies every acceptance criterion with roughly half the state. ADR impact: this is a user-visible defaulting behavior with subtle override semantics; a short ADR (or a section in docs/architecture.md capturing the override precedence rules and the "recent feed only" limitation) would prevent future regressions. Final challenge: if half the new architecture had to be removed, remove the baseline snapshot/restore mechanism and the `merchantInferenceRequested` re-application plumbing; keep the pure "infer on merchant change, respect manual flags" path. ```typescript categoryManuallySelected: false, cardManuallySelected: false, merchantInferenceRequested: false, inferredCategoryBaseline: undefined as { bucket: string; subcategory: string } | undefined, inferredCardBaseline: undefined as { card: string; custom: boolean; auto: boolean } | undefined, ```
Possible Issue `clearInferredDefaults` restores the pre-inference baseline whenever the merchant changes, but `categoryManuallySelected`/`cardManuallySelected` are not reset by `clearInferredDefaults`. Combined with the baseline being captured only via `??=`, a sequence like: select "Starbucks" (baseline captured, category inferred) -> manually pick a category (baseline cleared, flag set) -> select an unmatched merchant -> the flag stays true, so subsequent merchant selections never re-infer category for the rest of the transaction. This may be intended ("manual choice sticks for the transaction"), but it means the "restore prior selections when changing to an unmatched merchant" behavior and the manual-override behavior interact in a way that is hard to reason about and is not covered by a test for the manual-then-unmatched-then-known sequence. Worth confirming the intended precedence and adding a test. ```typescript clearInferredDefaults(): void { if (this.inferredCategoryBaseline) { this.parentBucket = this.inferredCategoryBaseline.bucket; this.subcategory = this.inferredCategoryBaseline.subcategory; this.inferredCategoryBaseline = undefined; } if (this.inferredCardBaseline) { this.card = this.inferredCardBaseline.card; this.isCustomCard = this.inferredCardBaseline.custom; this.autoCustomCard = this.inferredCardBaseline.auto; this.inferredCardBaseline = undefined; } }, ```
Data Mutation When history supplies a card not in `this.cards`, the code appends it to `this.cards` (`this.cards = [...this.cards, this.card]`). This mutates the card chip list based on inference rather than user action, and the appended card is not persisted here (persistCards is only called in the cards-load path). If the user then saves, the inferred card becomes a permanent chip; if they don't, the chip list is left in an inconsistent in-memory state. Consider whether inference should add chips at all, or only select an existing card, to avoid silently growing the card list from historical data. ```typescript this.card = historyCard; if (!this.cards.includes(this.card)) this.cards = [...this.cards, this.card]; ```

# Review: Merchant-Based Category and Card Defaults (#115)

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The core inference logic is reasonable and the test suite is unusually thorough for the happy paths and several race conditions. However, there are material correctness issues around state restoration, the manual-selection flag lifecycle, and the `isExactIntakeRule` heuristic that the tests do not exercise.

---

## Material Findings

### 1. HIGH — `clearInferredDefaults` restores stale baselines that were captured *after* a manual selection

**Evidence:** `selectBucket`/`selectSubcategory`/`selectCard`/`updateCustomCard`/`toggleCustomCard` all set `categoryManuallySelected = true` (or `cardManuallySelected = true`) and clear `inferredCategoryBaseline`/`inferredCardBaseline`. But `applyMerchantDefaults` only captures a baseline when `!this.categoryManuallySelected` / `!this.cardManuallySelected`. So far so good.

The problem is the *reset* path in `submitTransaction`:

```ts
if (this.isCustomMerchant) {
  this.clearInferredDefaults();
} else {
  this.inferredCategoryBaseline = undefined;
  this.inferredCardBaseline = undefined;
}
this.categoryManuallySelected = false;
this.cardManuallySelected = false;
```

For the non-custom-merchant branch, baselines are dropped but the *current* `parentBucket`/`subcategory`/`card` are **not** restored to their pre-inference values. That is intentional (you want to keep the inferred values for the next transaction at the same merchant — the test "retains inferred values for a second transaction" asserts this). Fine.

But consider the sequence: user selects merchant A (inference applies, baseline captured = defaults). User then manually selects a category (flag set, baseline cleared). User submits. On reset, `categoryManuallySelected = false`, baseline already `undefined`, and `parentBucket`/`subcategory` retain the *manual* values. Next transaction: user selects merchant B. `applyMerchantDefaults` now sees `!categoryManuallySelected` and captures a **new** baseline equal to the *previous transaction's manual category*. If the user then switches to an unknown merchant, `clearInferredDefaults` restores that stale manual category from the prior transaction.

**Failure scenario:** Transaction 1: pick "Trader Joe's", manually override to "Guilt-Free/Dining". Submit. Transaction 2: pick "Starbucks" (infers Guilt-Free/Coffee & Snacks, baseline = Guilt-Free/Dining). Switch to "Unknown Vendor" → category reverts to Guilt-Free/Dining, which was a *manual* choice from a *different* transaction, not a neutral default.

**Smallest robust fix:** On reset, when not custom-merchant, also reset `parentBucket`/`subcategory`/`card` to the form's canonical defaults (or re-derive from the newly-selected merchant) rather than leaving the previous transaction's values in place as the implicit baseline. Alternatively, capture the baseline at form-init time and restore to *that*, not to whatever the field held when inference first ran.

---

### 2. HIGH — `isExactIntakeRule` second clause is unsound

**Evidence:**

```ts
return (
  normalized.matchStrategy === "exact_rule" &&
  (normalized.canonicalMerchant.toLowerCase() === normalized.cleanedDescription.toLowerCase() ||
    Object.hasOwn(DEFAULT_CANONICAL_RULES, normalized.cleanedDescription))
);
```

`Object.hasOwn(DEFAULT_CANONICAL_RULES, normalized.cleanedDescription)` checks the *raw* cleaned description against the rule map keys. But `DEFAULT_CANONICAL_RULES` is keyed by canonical name (per the `CANONICAL_MERCHANT_RULES` construction: `rule.canonicalName.toLowerCase()`). The `cleanedDescription` is the *normalized input*, not the canonical name. These coincide only when the input already equals the canonical name. So this clause is either redundant with the first (when they match) or wrong (when `cleanedDescription` happens to equal some *other* rule's canonical name while `canonicalMerchant` is different — e.g., a shorter rule matched first).

The test "recognizes canonical merchant names even when a shorter rule matches first" (`Amazon Marketplace`) passes, but it passes via the *first* clause (`canonicalMerchant === cleanedDescription`), not the second. The second clause is dead-or-wrong code that gives false confidence.

**Failure scenario:** A merchant whose cleaned description equals rule X's canonical name but whose `matchStrategy` is `exact_rule` for a *different* rule Y (shorter match). The second clause returns true, `isExactIntakeRule` returns true, and `applyMerchantDefaults` treats it as an exact match — potentially applying Y's category while the history lookup uses X's canonical name. Inconsistent.

**Smallest robust fix:** Drop the second clause, or replace it with a check that the *matched rule's* canonical name equals the cleaned description (which is what the first clause already does). If the intent is "the input was already canonical," the first clause is sufficient.

---

### 3. MEDIUM — `merchantInferenceRequested` is not cleared on manual category/card selection, causing re-inference on late history load

**Evidence:** `loadRecentTransactions` ends with `if (this.merchantInferenceRequested) this.applyMerchantDefaults();`. `merchantInferenceRequested` is set in `selectMerchant` and `updateCustomMerchant` (when a match is found) and cleared only in `toggleCustomMerchant`, `updateCustomMerchant` (early return on empty), and `submitTransaction`.

If the user selects a merchant, then manually picks a category, then history arrives, `applyMerchantDefaults` runs again. The `categoryManuallySelected` guard prevents overwriting the category — good. But `applyMerchantDefaults` also re-runs the *card* inference and the `inferredCategoryBaseline ??=` capture. Since the baseline was cleared by the manual selection, a *new* baseline is captured from the current (manual) values. This compounds finding #1: the stale-baseline problem can be triggered by a late history load, not just by submit.

The test "uses history arriving after a merchant selection without overriding manual choices" covers the category case but not the baseline-capture side effect.

**Smallest robust fix:** Either (a) don't capture a baseline when `categoryManuallySelected`/`cardManuallySelected` is true (already the case for the *assignment*, but the `??=` capture happens inside the same `if (!this.categoryManuallySelected)` block — verify it does; it does, so this is actually guarded), or (b) more robustly, clear `merchantInferenceRequested` when a manual category/card selection is made, since the user has taken over. Option (b) also prevents redundant re-inference work.

Actually re-reading: the baseline capture *is* inside the `!this.categoryManuallySelected` guard, so finding #3's baseline concern is mitigated. The remaining concern is redundant re-inference and the card path: `if (!this.cardManuallySelected && historyCard)` — also guarded. So #3 reduces to: **redundant work and a subtle interaction with #1's reset path**. Downgrade to LOW-MEDIUM. Still worth clearing the flag on manual selection for clarity.

---

### 4. MEDIUM — `applyMerchantDefaults` mutates `this.cards` during inference, which can leak into `persistCards`

**Evidence:**

```ts
if (!this.cards.includes(this.card)) this.cards = [...this.cards, this.card];
```

This appends the inferred card to the card list. `persistCards` (called from `loadRecentTransactions`) writes `this.cards` to `localStorage`. So an inferred card from history gets persisted as if it were a user-known card. That's probably desirable (it *is* a card the user has used), but it means the inference has a side effect on persistent state. If the inferred card came from a malformed history entry (e.g., whitespace-only after trim — guarded by `historyCard` truthiness, OK; or a card that's actually a custom card string), it gets promoted to a first-class card.

**Failure scenario:** History contains `card: "  "` → `historyCard = ""` → guarded. History contains `card: "Other"` (a sentinel) → appended to `cards` and selected. Low likelihood but worth a guard.

**Smallest robust fix:** Only append to `this.cards` if the card passes the same validation used elsewhere (non-empty after trim, not a sentinel). Or accept the side effect and document it.

---

### 5. LOW — `normalizeIntakeMerchant` hardcodes `confidence: 0.98` and `requiresLLM: false`

**Evidence:** The override sets these fields unconditionally when a canonical rule matches. If `normalizeMerchant` already produced a higher-confidence or different result, this clobbers it. More importantly, `requiresLLM: false` is asserted without checking whether the rule actually resolves the merchant. For a rule that matched via a short token (the `Medium Rare` case), `requiresLLM` might legitimately be true.

**Failure scenario:** Downstream code that branches on `requiresLLM` (not visible in this diff) may skip LLM fallback for a merchant that only partially matched.

**Smallest robust fix:** Preserve `normalized.requiresLLM` unless the rule is an exact match; or set `requiresLLM: !isExactIntakeRule(...)`.

---

## Unverified Assumptions

- **`RecentTransaction` shape:** The diff imports `type RecentTransaction` from `intake-form.ts` and the test helper constructs it with `parent_bucket`, `subcategory`, `card`, `merchant`, etc. I cannot verify from the diff that `loadRecentTransactions` actually populates `recentTransactions` with this shape (the API response mapping is outside the diff). If the API returns `parentBucket` (camelCase) instead of `parent_bucket`, all history inference silently no-ops.
- **`CATEGORIES_BY_BUCKET` contents:** The guard `options?.includes(subcategory)` assumes `CATEGORIES_BY_BUCKET` is keyed by bucket and contains subcategory strings. Not shown in diff.
- **`DEFAULT_CANONICAL_RULES` key semantics:** The `CANONICAL_MERCHANT_RULES` map is built from `rule.canonicalName.toLowerCase()`, but `isExactIntakeRule` checks `Object.hasOwn(DEFAULT_CANONICAL_RULES, cleanedDescription)`. Whether `DEFAULT_CANONICAL_RULES` is keyed by canonical name, token, or something else is not visible. This directly affects finding #2.
- **`normalizeMerchant` behavior:** Whether it sets `matchStrategy: "exact_rule"` only for full-string matches or also for token matches is not visible. The `Medium Rare` test implies token matches exist, but the strategy value for them is unverified.
- **`this.allMerchants` population:** `updateCustomMerchant` checks `this.allMerchants.some(...)`. Whether `allMerchants` is populated before the user types (from `localStorage` on init) is not shown.

---

## Missing Verification

- **No test for the stale-baseline-after-submit scenario** (finding #1). The "allows new inference after saving a manual selection" test covers the flag reset but not the baseline restoration on a subsequent unknown-merchant switch.
- **No test for `isExactIntakeRule`'s second clause** in isolation. The `Amazon Marketplace` test passes via the first clause.
- **No test for `applyMerchantDefaults` being called twice** (once from `selectMerchant`, once from `loadRecentTransactions`) with a manual selection in between — the interaction between `merchantInferenceRequested` and the manual flags.
- **No test for `this.cards` mutation** during inference and its persistence.
- **No test for `requiresLLM` preservation.**
- **No test for the `isNegative && bucket === "Income"` guard** — the condition exists but no test exercises a negative-amount transaction with an Income-inferring merchant.

---

## ADR / Documentation Impact

The `docs/architecture.md` addition describes the behavior accurately for the happy path but omits:
- The baseline-restoration semantics (what happens when switching to an unknown merchant after inference).
- The fact that inference mutates `this.cards` and persists it.
- The `merchantInferenceRequested` flag's role in late-history re-inference.

If finding #1 is fixed by changing the reset semantics, the doc should state the new rule explicitly (e.g., "manual selections are preserved for the current transaction only; on submit, category and card reset to the inferred values for the selected merchant, or to form defaults if none").

---

## Final Challenge

**The strongest credible reason this change could still be wrong:** The `isExactIntakeRule` heuristic is the linchpin that prevents token-embedded false positives (the `Medium Rare` case), but its second clause (`Object.hasOwn(DEFAULT_CANONICAL_RULES, cleanedDescription)`) is checking the wrong key space. If `DEFAULT_CANONICAL_RULES` is keyed by *token* rather than *canonical name*, then the second clause is actually doing the opposite of what the comment claims — it would return true for any input whose cleaned description happens to equal a token, re-introducing the exact false-positive the function is meant to prevent. The tests don't distinguish these cases because the `Medium Rare` test relies on `matchStrategy` (first clause) and the `Amazon Marketplace` test relies on canonical-name equality (first clause). The second clause is untested and its correctness depends entirely on an unverified assumption about the rule map's key structure.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge]([redacted-url])</sub></sub>  Preserve the Income sign invariant when restoring defaults**

After saving an Income transaction, selecting an expense merchant such as Starbucks captures Income as the category baseline. If the user then enables credit mode and switches to an unmatched merchant (or opens Other), this restoration sets the bucket back to Income without clearing `isNegative`. The form can consequently enqueue a negative Income transaction, which `functions/api/transactions.ts` explicitly rejects. Restore the sign invariant here, as `selectBucket()` does, or avoid restoring Income while credit mode is active.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed in c51f37d263f0e2ded42810fee259b4ed7747fbb9. When credit mode is active, restoring an Income baseline now falls back to Guilt-Free / Dining and preserves the credit sign. Clearing the sign instead was rejected because it would silently change the user's credit into a positive expense. A regression test reproduces the Income-to-expense-to-credit-to-unknown sequence.

**🟠 High · Previous defaults carry over**

When a transaction with inferred category or card defaults is saved and the user then selects an unmatched merchant, `submitTransaction()` discards the inferred baselines while leaving the inferred values in place, so `clearInferredDefaults()` has nothing to restore and the previous merchant’s category and card remain selected for the next transaction. The user can save those values for the wrong merchant.

Restore the inferred category and card to their baselines before discarding those baselines.

The user can save those values for the wrong merchant.

Restore the inferred category and card to their baselines before discarding those baselines.
~~~

Fixed in 6d2d4577402ad953901d058425841f52d2a867fd. I retain inferred baselines after saving the selected merchant, so changing to a different unmatched merchant can restore the prior values. Restoring immediately after every save was rejected because it would erase useful defaults when entering another transaction for the same merchant.

**🟡 Medium · Refresh replaces selected merchant**

When the user selects a merchant absent from the server list, submits, and the pending merchant-list response arrives afterward, `submitTransaction()` clears `merchantInferenceRequested` while a merchant-list request is still pending, so its response skips the selected-chip preservation block and replaces a selected merchant missing from the server list with the first frequent merchant. The next entry is left on a different merchant.

Preserve the selected merchant independently of the per-transaction inference flag, or invalidate the pending list response when submission resets form state.

A separate merchantUserSelected flag preserves the chip selection across a pending merchant-list refresh even after per-transaction inference state resets. Invalidating the request on submit was rejected because it would make selection correctness depend on request timing.
